The Matryoshka objective is a **plain sum of the PAIR loss computed at four prefix dimensions: 200, 256, 512, and 1024** (p. 5).

**Formulation (Eq. 6, p. 5)**

L = Σ_{d ∈ D} L_PAIR^(d), where D = {200, 256, 512, 1024}

- L_PAIR^(d) is the PAIR loss computed using only the first d embedding dimensions (p. 5).
- The PAIR loss is a multi-negative objective. It takes the log-softmax of the clicked candidate's score against K negatives (Eq. 2, p. 5). Each score is cosine similarity divided by a temperature τ (Eq. 1, p. 4), and τ = 0.02 in all experiments (p. 6).

**Weighting**

The per-dimension losses are added with no weighting coefficients, so each prefix contributes equally (Eq. 6, p. 5). The paper does not discuss or tune alternative weightings.

**Why these dimensions**

- **200:** approximates the storage footprint of the production 171-dimensional Holistic embedding (p. 5).
- **256, 512, 1024:** progressively higher-quality serving configurations (p. 5).

**Result**

One model is trained, and at serving time its embeddings can be truncated to the target dimension without retraining (pp. 5–6). Truncated versions score as follows on MAR@100 (Table 3, p. 8):

| Dimensions | MAR@100 |
|---|---|
| 200 | 0.421 |
| 256 | 0.432 |
| 512 | 0.444 |
| 1024 | 0.450 |
